title: People Began to Call on God

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Seth also had a son, and he named him Enosh. At that time people began to call on the name of the Lord. - Gen 4:26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What a beautiful note to end the chapter on. After all the wandering and violence of Cain's line, here in Seth's line something wonderful begins: "people began to call on the name of the Lord." This is the first mention of public worship, of people gathering to seek God, pray to Him, and depend on Him openly. In the midst of a darkening world, a stream of true faith starts to flow.

Two lines have now emerged in Genesis - Cain's line, building cities and songs without God, and Seth's line, calling on the Lord. Two directions the human heart can take. And it is through this praying, God-seeking line that the Saviour of the world would eventually come.

There is deep encouragement here. No matter how dark the surrounding culture becomes, God always preserves a people who call on His name. You may feel you are surrounded by a world that has forgotten God - but the remnant of faith never disappears. God keeps it alive in every generation.

And the invitation still stands: "Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved" (Rom 10:13). That is the simplest and most glorious response to everything Genesis 4 has shown us. In a world of Cains and Lamechs, we can be people who call on the Lord.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you someone who regularly calls on the name of the Lord?
- How can you help keep true worship alive in your family and community?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, in a world that so often forgets You, make me one who calls on Your name. Thank You that everyone who calls on You is saved.
